tei:titleStmt.tei:title: אִיתְגַּבַּר
Itgabar — a targum-piyyuṭ for introducing the sixth of the ten commandments on Shavuot

tei:div.tei:head: Itgabar — a targum-piyyuṭ for introducing the sixth of the ten commandments on Shavuot

tei:lg.tei:l: Adonijah son of Ḥaggit strengthened in power,
when Joab son of Ẓeruiah came in his cunning.
Between the mountains shouted Joab,
and all creatures heard his voice.
“Great am I, none is like me,
but what benefit is all my greatness to me?
Doesn’t King Solomon sit on the throne, thinking to kill me,
unwilling to hear my voice’s words?
Ere all the good I did with David his father,
did King Solomon recall it on my behalf?
When forts and ports I conquered before him,
rivers, ocean, and all dry land?
Zipped away from me all the great ones,
and all the warrior fled from before me!
How shameful upon this world, if this is the rule,
that a warrior like me be killed by the sword!”
Tasting the taste of death, Joab,
when he heard them saying “Come on, let’s kill him!”
“Nice. Your rule is to kill me,
after I killed all your enemies!”
Consequently when Joab saw they would kill him,
he started shouting for Joel his son.
“Look, Joel, my son, I’m ordering you:
keep the Torah, raise your brothers, honor your mother.
Me, what can I do against King Solomon?
How is he so cruel as to kill me?”
Now at that time Joab roared,
and his voice was heard in all the land of Israel.
“Suffer yourself not to kill me,
for a day will come when you will remember me.”
Opined King Solomon,
“Remember Abner son of Ner’s blood?
Does Amasa son of Jether not cross your mind?”
Prying open his mouth, Joab son of Zeruiah
went and cried with all his friends.
Screamed Joab at that time,
and all the warriors took up their arms.
Quickened was King Solomon by his voice,
and he started shouting for Rehoboam his son.
“Rehoboam my son! Get up, draw your weapon,
and remember your uncle Absalom’s blood!”
Shed tears began to flow from their eyes,
as all Israel heard his voice.
Thus Solomon was shocked and said in his heart,
“What is to be done of my father’s oath?”
When Joab son of Zeruiah heard,
prying open his mouth Joab started to shout for Benaiah son of Jehoiada.
“Benaiah! Benaiah! Don’t let it cross your mind!
Chunky is my neck, your sword is weak, and you cannot kill me!”
Quickly, Benaiah sliced off Joab’s head,
and Joab’s head rushed to King Solomon’s house.
Shouting with joy were the peoples
when they heard Joab was dead, but their hearts wept.
Thus Israel shook and wept great tears,
that Joab son of Zeruiah was killed.

tei:note.tei:p: In the Paris National Library 606 manuscript, everything from here to the third-to-last-line is replaced with an alternate shorter text: “עֲנֵה וַאֲמַר לְיוֹאֵל בְּרֵיה לְאִימָּךְ תְּיַקַר וְלָא־כַּעֲבַדְתְּ בְּחַיָּי וְאָחוּךְ תִּיזוּן וְלָא־תִּשְׁבּוֹק יָתְהוֹן מַה עֲבַד לִי מַלְכָּא שְׁלֹמֹה בְּדִינִין אַכְזָרַאִין דָּן יָתִי נְהַם יוֹאָב בְּהַהִיא שַׁעְתָּא וְכׇל־גִּיבָּרִין אָחְדוּ זֵינֵיהוֹן סְבוֹל גַּרְמָךְ וְלָא תִּקְטוֹל יָתִי עֲתִיד לְמִמְטֵיךְ זְמַן דְּתִדְכַּר יָתִי עִיוְתֵיהּ דְּאַבְנֵר בֶּן־נֵר לָא־תִדְכַּר לִי וְדַעֲמָשָׂא בֶּן־יֶתֶר לָא־תִּשְׁבַּק רוּחִי פְּתַח פּוּמֵיהּ יוֹאָב וַאֲמַר לִקְטוֹלֵיהּ בְּנָיָה בְּנָיָה הֵיךְ תִּקְטוֹל יָתִי צַוָּארִי תְּקֵיף וְסַיְפָךְ חֲלַשׁ וְהֵיךְ אַתְּ יָכִיל לִי לְמִקְטְלִי קִיצֵּץ בְּנָיָה רֵישֵׁיהּ דְּיוֹאָב וְאַעִיל יָתֵיה לְבֵי מַלְכָּא שְׁלֹמֹה רַעֲדוּ וְאִיתְבְּהִילוּ כׇּל־גִּיבָּרִין וּבְכוֹ כׇּל־רַבְרְבָנֵי דְּמַלְכָּא שָׁמְעוּ...” (...he called for and said to Joel his son: “Let your mother be honored, not like you did in my life, and care for your brothers, do not abandon them. My, what did King Solomon do to me? With cruel laws he judged me!”Now Joab roared at that time, and all the warriors grabbed their weapons, “Suffer my existence, do not kill me! To you time will come when you remember me! Of Abner son of Ner’s error do not recall against me, nor take my life for Amasa son of Jether!” Prying open his mouth, Joab said to his killer, “Benaiah! Benaiah! How will you kill me? Chunky is my neck, your sword is weak, and how can you chance to kill me? Quickly Benaiah cut off Joab;’s head, and brought it to the house of King Solomon. Rattled, all the warriors were shaken, and all the king’s great ones wept. Shouting...)
A name found nowhere earlier to this poem for the son of Joab.
Some texts say כַּד חֲמָא גִּיבָּרַיָּא דְּאָחְדִין זֵינֵיהוֹן when the warriors saw that they were holding their weapons
Some texts say בְּשַׁעְתֵּיהּ הַהִיא at his time
Some texts say וְאִישְׁתְּמַע קָלֵיהּ בְּכׇל־אַרְעָא and his voice was heard in all the land
Older texts conclude here in medias res. The remaining lines, found in later texts, conclude the story.
The nations, who were his enemy, but respected his courage.
